title: Colocation scale scenario matrix — power, cooling, and rack allocation (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scenario matrix and operational planning note for rapid GPU pod scale in colocation and on-prem sites through Q2–Q4 2026. Aim: provide a compact decision matrix for power/cooling headroom, floor/rack allocation, and rollout phasing across candidate sites (SFO-1, IAD-2, FRA-1).

Context and constraints:
- Business asks: support +6k sustained A100-equivalent GPUs by end of 2026 across hosted & private pools, with regional minimums for redundancy.
- Time horizon: 6–12 months (fast ramp).
- Typical node target: 4x A100-80GB equivalent per chassis (actual hardware mix may include 8x smaller GPUs later).
- Design principle: prefer conservative electrical and thermal headroom to avoid mid-deployment remediation.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Average sustained draw per full GPU node: 2.8 kW (includes fans, NICs, DC-DC overhead).
- Typical 42U rack density: 10–14 full nodes depending on chassis; plan for 12 nodes/rack baseline.
- Baseline per-rack deliverable power (colo): 20 kW. Target higher-density racks at 25 kW where available.
- PUE target at site: 1.3 (good-medium); adjust cooling margin if PUE >1.4 observed.
- Utility redundancy: N+1 at room level, with critical racks on dedicated PDUs backed by generator UPS.

Scenario matrix (conservative / baseline / aggressive):
1) Node-level assumptions:
   - Conservative: node draw 3.2 kW, 10 nodes/rack -> 32 kW needed => only possible in 25–40 kW racks (rare), flag high risk.
   - Baseline: node draw 2.8 kW, 12 nodes/rack -> 33.6 kW -> we must split across two PDUs or use specialized high-density racks; not realistic in 20 kW racks.
   - Operational approach: target 8–12 nodes per standard rack (20 kW); push denser pods (25 kW) only in specially provisioned aisles.

2) Rack counts per region (goal: 2k GPUs per region baseline):
   - SFO-1 (edge+hosted): Baseline estimate: 170 racks (12 nodes/rack -> ~2,040 nodes capacity). Plan buffer +20% => 204 racks.
   - IAD-2 (primary east): Baseline estimate: 180 racks, buffer +15% => 207 racks.
   - FRA-1 (eu): Baseline estimate: 120 racks, buffer +25% => 150 racks (smaller initial footprint).
   Notes: these numbers assume mixing dense and standard racks; actual rack count will drop if we move to more efficient chassis or mix in 8-GPU nodes.

Simple power budget table (baseline):
- SFO-1: average power per rack (delivered) 20 kW -> 204 racks -> 4.08 MW delivered; plus 10% colo overhead and PDU losses -> ~4.5 MW site draw.
- IAD-2: 207 racks -> 4.14 MW delivered -> ~4.56 MW site draw.
- FRA-1: 150 racks -> 3.0 MW delivered -> ~3.3 MW site draw.
Total baseline draw (delivered to racks): ~11.22 MW (approx 12.36 MW site).

Cooling and chiller margins:
- Convert electrical to thermal load at ~0.9 factor (loss to servers etc.).
- Baseline thermal load SFO: ~3.6 MW heat to remove (after PUE adjustments). Ensure chiller capacity >= baseline * 1.25 for safety.
- Recommendation: require vendor confirmation of chilled water delta-T and CRAC capacity when locking contracts; prefer sites with documented hot-aisle containment and overhead cooling risers.

Floor allocation guidance and aisle planning:
- Reserve contiguous aisle blocks in multiples of 12 racks to simplify power/cooling trunking.
- For sites with 20 kW PDUs, plan for 8–10 nodes per rack; if we intend 12 nodes/rack we must secure 25 kW per-rack cabinets or split power across two circuits with separate PDUs.
- Cater for cable management corridors: ~1.5m service corridor per row for air handling and servicing.

Electrical robustness checklist (for colo ops):
- Confirm per-rack breaker size, PDU rating, and whether PDUs support dynamic load shedding (recommended).
- Verify ATS (automatic transfer switch) test schedule and generator load tests in contract.
- Ask colo for past incident logs (transient outages in last 24 months).

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: underestimated per-node draw -> mitigation: lock sample nodes on-site, measure at full load before racking. Owner: Jonah Kim.
- Risk: cooling insufficiency -> mitigation: require chiller headroom or portable chiller commitment. Owner: Sofia Patel.
- Risk: lead time on high-density cabinets -> mitigation: pre-book special racks 90 days ahead. Owner: Luke Andersen.

Staging and rollout phasing (recommended):
Phase 0: validation (2–4 weeks)
- Ship 2 racks to each target site with production-calibrated nodes. Run 72h soak at peak schedule to validate power draw and thermal behavior.
Phase 1: initial capacity (4–8 weeks)
- Deploy 20% of baseline racks, verify telemetry and PUE numbers, enable remote PDU monitoring.
Phase 2: scale (8–20 weeks)
- Bulk racking in 2–4 week waves, staggered by aisle to allow incremental chiller tuning.
Phase 3: steady state
- Move to autoscaling pools and operational playbooks for failover.

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Per-rack: inlet/outlet temperature probes (min 2 per rack), PDU per-phase current sensors, per-rack humidity probe.
- Site: aggregate PUE reporting, chiller runtime, ATS events, emergency cooling vent status.
- Integrations: webhook to infra-alerting; long-term retention for capacity trending (90 days hot, 2 years cold).

Open questions (to resolve before vendor sign-off):
- Which chassis/node models are we locking for the Q3 procurement window? (affects rack density).
- Colo billing model: flat kW vs. kWh + demand charge — which is more cost-predictable for us? Finance input required (see INFRA-9821).
- Is the site capable of 3-phase 480V distribution with per-rack step-down transformer?

Immediate next actions (owners & ETA):
- Jonah: schedule onsite rack power soak tests at SFO-1, target week of 2026-03-15.
- Sofia: compile chiller capacity reports for candidate colo sites, due 2026-03-22.
- Luke: confirm procurement lead times for 25 kW cabinets and PDUs, due 2026-03-19.
- Riley (owner): finalize scenario matrix and prep vendor RFP template, due 2026-03-26.

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc intentionally mixes top-line capacity math with operational notes. Treat as working doc; final numbers to be produced after hardware definition and soak tests.
- If you have site-specific floor plans or recent PUE audits, paste links into the confluence page referenced in linked_artifacts.

Revision history: 
- 2026-02-12: initial draft (Riley)
- 2026-02-24: added regional rack estimates and power table (Luke)
- 2026-03-05: appended rollout phasing and telemetry checklist (Sofia)

END.
